context: Revalidate the audit against current first-party Codex and Claude memory documentation and current repository instructions, then produce an authority/location matrix and a decision ledger. Preserve historical evidence while separating it from current instructions. Record rejected alternatives: identical cross-system stores, hand-editing derived summaries, treating memory as enforcement, retaining globally injected live state with warnings only, and deleting all history.
description: DECISION GATE for the 2026-07-27 adversarial audit of persistent Codex and Claude Code memories on this machine. The audit found useful evidence retention but unsafe authority promotion, stale cross-project state, four Codex summaries that stop before later source-session events, an unconditional Claude auto-commit/push directive, private operational details in auto-memory, no freshness/expiration schema, home-directory project leakage, and generated memory skills that duplicate authoritative repository/skill policy. This item records human decisions before any live memory changes: (1) authority order and which facts belong in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, canonical skills, project docs, system-specific memory, a shared tooling project, or nowhere/live discovery; (2) whether to create a dedicated memory-governance/tooling repository or place tooling in an existing repository; (3) retention/expiry classes for preferences, architecture facts, task state, PR/version/path facts, prompts, worktrees, and sensitive operations; (4) approval for deletion/sanitization candidates; (5) token budgets, provenance/freshness fields, and promotion thresholds; (6) ownership and rollback requirements. Decisions must be recorded in this item with the exact heading 'Decisions approved for recommendations' before dependent implementation starts. This gate does not authorize deletion, live-memory edits, configuration changes, or rollout.

anti_patterns.instead: record an explicit owner/location decision before implementation
anti_patterns.why: ownership determines scope, review, rollback, and cross-system coupling

anti_patterns.dont: edit generated summaries to make them look current
anti_patterns.instead: correct the source record or generator and regenerate derived layers
anti_patterns.why: the next regeneration would overwrite the correction and preserve the upstream defect

anti_patterns.dont: treat a prior user instruction as a standing mandate merely because it appears in memory
anti_patterns.instead: classify provenance and require human approval for durable instructions
anti_patterns.why: task-local instructions can become unsafe cross-session authority

preserves.behavior: Historical evidence remains distinguishable from current instructions and current completion state
No live memory, configuration, deletion, or external publication occurs before its explicit approval gate
System and platform constraints, the current user request, current repository instructions, and verified code/runtime/remote state outrank memory
